patch.summary: Configure a heat, booked or not (name, style, product limit)
patch.description: Locates a heat by track + heatStart (booked heats match on the track word in their name; virgin heats — named "Heat <n>" — match via the track's resource id), then applies two independent operations, either or both of which may be requested. Sending { level, junior } derives and applies the heat's display name and style; omitting both leaves name and style untouched. Sending `productLimitId` locks that product limit on the heat (omit it to leave the limit unchanged). On virgin heats the limit's name is appended to the derived heat name (e.g. "33 - Mega Pro - Lock Race"), or becomes the whole name when no level/junior was sent (e.g. "33 - Lock Race"), until a booking rewrites it. A product-limit-only call is how a slot is fenced for website sale before anyone has booked it. Name and style are derived from HeadPinz's heat-naming scheme ("# - Track [Junior] Level"), so they always stay aligned. post.summary: Place a racer in a heat with a pending $0 sale (kiosk / web, no reservation)
post.description: Puts a person into a BMI heat and opens the $0 sale the till would open, without a reservation. The heat is configured from the entry if it is still on the day template (setup swapped, named '<number> - <entry>'), the participant is inserted with the entry's speed class, then BL_OPEN opens a bill with no project and one entry line is written with the racer as payer and consumer, attributed to BMI's PUBLIC API identity -- the exact shape of the till's own walk-in sales. The bill stays open (kind 0) so `paid` reads false: this is the pending state. POST .../participant/{participantId}/pay marks it paid; DELETE .../participant/{participantId} cancels an unpaid one. Pass paid=true to place and pay in one call. Only $0 entry products are ever put on the line; a priced product is refused. Idempotent on the racer: someone already in the heat returns 200 with their existing participant and bill. Before opening a sale, an unclaimed entry line the racer already has from the current workday (06:00 to 06:00) is reused -- a racer cancelled after paying today, or an entry the till rang through today -- and the response says so with sold=false; such a line may already be paid. That endpoint resolves a named `agent` by substring-matching it against each member's `name` (`firstName lastName`, case-sensitive) and fails the whole lead with 500 when nobody matches, so a CRM can read this first and show which planners a center will actually accept instead of losing a guest's lead. Read-only: this touches nothing in BMI. 404 when the Square location has no `bmiAddress` (no BMI server to ask).

post.summary: Scan the AV network for nodes through the location's Q-SYS Core
post.description: Asks the Control Script on the location's Q-SYS Core (qsys/avoip-discovery.lua, port 8002) to find the HDTV encoder / decoder nodes now and returns the list when the scan finishes, normally about 3 seconds. The Core is on the AV network, so it can use the nodes' multicast group or sweep the subnet, neither of which Pandora can do from Azure. Each device carries its ip, device id (the devid to use as an encoder source), user-set name, a kind heuristic (encoder / decoder / unknown), HDMI input state, output resolution, and encoding settings where the node answered. The Core address is resolved from the location's qsysAddress custom attribute.
